title: Personal Information Leakage During Registration
description: During account registration, personal information (name, contact details, device credentials) could be leaked through insecure data transmission, storage vulnerabilities, or unauthorized access to the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Assumes registration data is transmitted over network and stored on Home Hub

title: Unintended Disclosure of Enrolled Devices
description: Camera/sensor enrollment data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or lack of access controls during the enrollment process.
assumptions: Assumes enrollment data includes device identifiers and access credentials

title: Lack of Control Over Collected Data
description: Homeowner may lack control over how their registration data and enrolled device information is used, shared, or retained after the initial enrollment process.
assumptions: Assumes data collection continues beyond initial registration

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The registration and enrollment process may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding data collection, consent, and user rights.
assumptions: Assumes registration involves collection of personal data subject to privacy regulations

title: Access Code Leakage During Entry
description: Guest may inadvertently expose the temporary access code through visible screen display, audible speech, or improper logging during code entry at the Home Hub.
assumptions: Code entry interface may not have proper input masking or secure transmission

title: Unauthorized Access via Weak Code
description: Guest may use a weak or predictable temporary access code that could be guessed or compromised by unauthorized parties attempting to access the front door.
assumptions: Temporary access codes may be short or easily guessable

title: Inability to Detect Unauthorized Door Access Attempts
description: Home Hub may not properly detect or log unauthorized access attempts to the front door, making it difficult to identify security breaches or suspicious behavior.
assumptions: System may lack comprehensive logging or monitoring capabilities for door access events

title: Unintended Door Access Consequences
description: Temporary access code may be used by unauthorized parties or in unintended circumstances, leading to door access when it should not be granted.
assumptions: Code validation may not include sufficient checks for legitimate guest status or time validity

title: Data Loss During Storage
description: Motion/door/sensor events written to the local event log may be lost due to hardware failure, storage corruption, or accidental deletion, resulting in incomplete event records.
assumptions: The local event log relies on local storage without redundant backup mechanisms.

title: Unauthorized Access to Event Log
description: An attacker with physical or network access to the home hub could potentially read or modify the local event log contents, compromising event privacy.
assumptions: The local event log is accessible to the home hub and potentially other devices on the same network.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Data
description: Motion/door/sensor events stored in the local event log could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data leakage.
assumptions: The local event log may be accessible to unauthorized users or systems without proper authentication.

title: Unintended Data Flow to External Systems
description: Event data written to the local event log may be inadvertently accessed or transmitted to external systems without proper authorization or consent.
assumptions: The local event log may be accessible to other devices or services on the home network.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Storage and handling of motion/door/sensor events in the local event log may violate privacy regulations or data protection requirements.
assumptions: The local event log may not comply with applicable data protection regulations regarding personal data handling.

title: Data Loss During Upload
description: Camera clips may be lost during the upload process from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage due to network failures, server crashes, or transmission errors.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure During Upload
description: Camera clips may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the upload process due to insecure transmission channels or misconfigured upload settings.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video Clips
description: Cloud Video Storage may allow unauthorized access to uploaded camera clips due to weak access controls or misconfigured storage permissions.

title: Data Unavailability During Storage
description: Cloud Video Storage may become unavailable during the upload process or after storage due to service outages, maintenance, or technical failures.

title: Unauthorized Deletion of Video Clips
description: Cloud Video Storage may allow unauthorized deletion of uploaded camera clips due to weak access controls or misconfigured storage permissions.

title: Motion-detected notification may disclose sensitive home activity information
description: The notification sent to the homeowner may reveal sensitive information about when someone is present in the home, unusual activity patterns, or security events that could be misused by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The notification contains data about motion detection events that could indicate occupancy or security incidents.

title: Notification may contain more information than necessary
description: The motion-detected notification may include more detailed information than required for the intended purpose of alerting the homeowner, potentially exposing unnecessary data about home activity.
assumptions: The notification includes timestamp, location, and activity details that exceed what is needed for basic motion alerting.

title: Homeowner may lack control over notification settings
description: The homeowner may not have adequate control over when, how, or whether they receive motion-detected notifications, potentially leading to privacy concerns or notification fatigue.
assumptions: Notification settings are not easily configurable or are not transparent to the homeowner.

title: Notification may be sent to unintended recipient
description: The motion-detected notification may be sent to the wrong homeowner or to multiple homeowners when only one should receive it, potentially causing privacy breaches.
assumptions: There is a risk of misconfiguration in the notification routing system.

title: Unauthorized Access to Shared Analytics Data
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) may access the aggregated device-usage analytics beyond the intended scope, potentially exposing more user information than necessary or allowing unauthorized third-party access to the data once it reaches the vendor.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Sharing
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may have unintended consequences, such as the vendor using the data for purposes beyond the original agreement, or the data being used to infer sensitive user information not originally intended to be shared.

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: The data sharing with the cloud analytics vendor may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent mechanisms are not in place, or if the vendor is not properly vetted for compliance with applicable data protection laws.

title: Data Loss During Transmission
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may be lost or corrupted during transmission from the mobile app backend (P2) to the cloud analytics vendor (EE3), potentially resulting in incomplete or inaccurate analytics data.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be retained longer than necessary for the intended purpose, violating the storage limitation principle. Videos could be kept indefinitely without proper retention policies.

title: Unauthorized access to stored video data
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be accessed by unauthorized parties through compromised credentials, weak authentication, or security vulnerabilities in the storage system.

title: Data destruction during retrieval
description: Video data may be corrupted or lost during the retrieval process from cloud storage to mobile app backend, potentially resulting in incomplete or unavailable playback.

title: Unintended access during playback
description: Video clips retrieved by the mobile app backend may be accessed by unauthorized users if authentication controls are insufficient during playback.
